column4: This verse identifies the disbelievers as deniers before 84:24's warning and 84:25's exception; its own contribution is the opposing stance to the believing group whose uncut reward the section cites.

The section defines أجر as the return for a good act; in the same charity passage as 2:262-64, 2:261 pictures spending for God multiplying like grain with seven ears, making abundance a concrete form of returned reward.

The section reads a reward free of minnah as one that does not burden its recipient; this verse says spending is for God's face and will be repaid fully without wrong, joining unclaimed giving to complete recompense.
The section's dictionary definition of أجر allows recompense in this life or the next; 4:134 states that both kinds of reward are with God, making that twofold scope explicit.

The section's B003 dictionary note on حسن connects doing good with the best and more as reward; this verse says those who do good have al-husna and ziyada, extending the reward beyond the deed's return.
The section moves from humanity's best form to a downward line; this verse says long life can reverse a person in creation, ننكسه في الخلق, giving that decline a direct bodily formulation.

The section promises a wage that is not diminished; amid migration, hardship, fighting, and death, this verse says God will not let any worker's work be lost, tying costly actions to preserved recompense.
The section denies that reward is cut or reduced; this verse promises the patient a reward without account, adding the distinct idea of a return beyond ordinary reckoning.
